articleTitle: A Novel Integrated Approach for Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: For a sustainable environment, countries are planning to increase the share of Renewable Energy Resources (RERs) in their energy mix. Wind is the type of RERs that has the potential to overcome fossil reserves. However, due to the uncertain nature of wind, its integration with existing power systems brings instability. This instability can be overcome by implementing some accurate wind power forecasting techniques. Therefore, in this proposed study, we present a novel integrated approach for hour-ahead wind power forecasting. The proposed approach has two levels. At level 1, three boosting algorithms: Extreme Gradient Boosting (XgBoost), Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), and Random Forest (RF) are implemented. Level 2 consists of Linear Regression (LR) which adjusts the weights and biases and gives an hour-ahead forecast. The datasets of two different wind turbines are used in this study. For the robustness analysis, the proposed approach is compared with the XgBoost, CatBoost, RF, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks. The findings demonstrate that the proposed integrated approach outperforms other models. For the Texas turbine dataset, the proposed approach records improvement of 11.51% and 39.1% in MAE than XgBoost, and CatBoost models, respectively. In the case of Turkey turbine dataset, the MAE of the proposed integrated network is 1.9% and 26.65% better than the MAE recorded by XgBoost, and CatBoost models. respectively.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm-Optimized PID for Enhanced Power System Stability: A Comparative Evaluation with Pole Placement in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Ensuring stable and optimal power system performance is paramount for reliable energy grid operation. This study comprehensively explores and compares four control strategies for Load Frequency Control (LFC) in interconnected power systems. Cases include operating without a controller (Case 1), employing Conventional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control (Case 2), utilizing Pole Placement (Case 3), and implementing Genetic Algorithm (GA)-optimized PID control (Case 4). Utilizing a dynamic system model with parameters from an isolated power station, the study observes system responses to sudden load changes and resulting frequency deviations. While Conventional PID (Case 2) demonstrates improvement, GA-optimized PID (Case 4) emerges as highly effective, show-casing minimal overshoot, rapid settling time, and enhanced peak values. The Pole Placement technique (Case 3) provides a comparative evaluation, revealing that GA-optimized PID excels in precise control. This analysis highlights trade-offs in control strategies, offering valuable insights for optimizing power system stability in interconnected grids and paving the way for further exploration of Intelligent control strategies.

articleTitle: 2-Bit Binary Encoded Plasmonic Wire Grating Metasurface for Absorption Enhancement of Kesterite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: This article presents and validates a process for increasing the energy conversion efficiency of copper zinc tin sulfide (CZTS) solar cells by placing a 2-bit binary encoded metasurface of plasmonic wire grating on top of the solar cell. The presented unit cell consisted of gold nanorods placed on top of a polymer TOPAS which is placed on top of the CZTS solar cell with a molybdenum ground plate. The numerical simulations for the presented model are carried out on COMSOL. The theoretical results acquired through numerical simulations presented satis-factory results that validate that the binary-encoded plasmonic wire grating increased the absorbance of the incident light. The different encoded metasurfaces presented maximum absorbance in different wavelength spectrums of solar irradiance, making them suitable candidates for different applications.

articleTitle: The Development of a Platform for Assessing Real-Time Dynamic Thermal Rating for the Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: The importance of Real-Time Thermal Rating (RTTR) lies in its crucial role within modern power transmission systems as it provides a dynamic and datadriven approach to assessing the thermal performance of overhead transmission lines. In this study, an RTTR platform is developed to enhance the reliability and efficiency of power transmission systems. Real-time weather data, line parameters and location information are employed by the platform to estimate the current thermal ratings of overhead transmission lines. A comparison of the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed platform with those of the conventional static thermal rating method is conducted, and critical spans are identified to ensure minimum electrical clearance, prioritizing the safety of both individuals and equipment. The developed web-based RTTR platform has the potential to grant power transmission system operators proactive management tools, representing a substantial advancement over traditional static thermal rating methods.

articleTitle: Evaluation, Selection and Simulation of Maximum Power Point Tracking Algorithm for LEO Satellite Electrical Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Energy is a premium resource in the world of on-board satellite communications. Most of the energy in space is generated from solar panels. But unfortunately, solar energy isn't always available during different phases of a satellite's orbit/trajectory. As a result, the on-board batteries kick-in during solar eclipse and provide the required power to satellite subsystems. Thus it is paramount that the batteries be replenished quickly and efficiently during the sun-lit phase. The satellite Electrical Power Sub-system (EPS) is responsible for providing, managing and replenishing this energy. Methods like Direct Energy Transfer (DET) and Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) are used to optimally interface/manage the EPS load. This work gauges the merits and demerits of satellite EPS operation using DET and MPPT for the proposed LEO orbital configurations and the one best suited for the considered mission profile is selected. A mission specific MATLAB/Simulink-based model is also developed to test and evaluate the performance of various MPPT techniques (e.g., P&O, IC, FOCV, FSCC, etc.) for our orbital/load requirements. Furthermore, performance comparison of these techniques is also evaluated based on a-priori mission requirements such as prior tuning, dynamic and steady-state tracking, algorithm/hardware complexity and sensor requirements. Based on these performance parameters and the simulation results (i.e. steady-state voltage fluctuations), P&O MPPT technique is selected for our rapidly varying satellite orbital conditions.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis and Design Optimization of 100kw Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine for Mitigating the Energy Crisis in Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Wind energy has emerged as a promising renewable energy source, offering sustainable and clean energy. However, maximizing wind turbine efficiency and costeffectiveness remains a critical challenge. This research focuses on the design and parametric analysis of a horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) with a target power output of 100 kW at a wind velocity of 10m/s. The study employs a comprehensive approach that encompasses parametric analysis of various airfoil geometries and angles of attack using Ansys Workbench, and Q-blade coupled with an in-depth evaluation of economic factors. The research commences the investigation of different airfoil profiles, including NACA 2412, S 1020, and K 3311. These airfoils are subjected to a parametric analysis, examining their performance characteristics across a range of angles of attack. The analysis utilizes computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to assess the lift and drag coefficients of each airfoil. In parallel with the airfoil analysis, the economic aspects of the HAWT design are carefully considered. Cost-benefit analysis is employed to evaluate various design parameters, such as blade material selection, and manufacturing processes. In conclusion, the research provides a comprehensive framework for designing a 100 kW HAWT that optimizes power output while maintaining economic viability. The study's findings offer valuable insights for wind energy practitioners and researchers, contributing to the advancement of wind turbine technology and the realization of sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Secure Federated Learning for UAV Swarms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have been recently leveraged in massive amount of Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, given the stringent limitations of UAVs, investigating their performance in terms of their energy efficiency, tasks accuracy, and security has gained much interest recently. In this paper, we study the deployment of Federated Learning (FL) within the UAV swarms, with the aim of avoiding data exchange between different swarm's members. Specifically, we propose a secure FL framework for UAV swarms, such that the energy efficiency is maximized, while enhancing the learning performance. The suggested approach takes into account the issue of data imbalance in FL in addition to the strict energy and security limits placed on the UAVs.Our findings show how effective our framework is in terms of security, energy efficiency, and classification accuracy when compared to baseline systems that don't take security or data imbalance into account.

articleTitle: A Novel Line Frequency Chopper-Based Rectifier With Input Filter for Enhanced Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: We have previously proposed a hybrid rectifier that consists of a diode rectifier and a series chopper that operates at the line frequency with the input current total harmonic distortion (THD) of 16.4% and 28% at the primary and secondary side, respectively, of a balanced three-phase transformer. This paper focuses on further reduction of the input current THD using an input LC filter. Generally, an LC filter at the input of a diode rectifier reduces the input current THD, however, it introduces a lagging phase as well resulting in a reduced power factor. To mitigate the lagging power factor, the proposed rectifier can be operated with a leading phase controllable through the switching angle of the series chopper. Hence, an appropriate design of an input LC filter reduces the input current THD without degrading the input power factor. The proposed approach is presented with simulations and hardware results showing a significant reduction in the input current THD to 7% with a displacement factor close to unity.

articleTitle: Real-Time Non-Gaussianity Evaluation for Anomaly Detection in Noisy Power Grid Data Stream
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: In response to concerns regarding energy sustainability and increasing energy demand, a substantial number of renewable energy systems (RESs) are being integrated into the power grid. Unlike conventional power plants that can be adjusted to meet demand, RESs rely on weather conditions, introducing numerous unstable factors and abnormal events. Anomaly detection is a critical data analysis task, beneficial for pinpointing grid irregularities, failures, or intrusions. By examining anomaly patterns in integrated energy systems, a deeper comprehension of their operational status can be attained, leading to enhanced reliability and efficiency of the power grid. This paper suggests a statistical algorithm based on assessing nonGaussianity. In contrast to computationally expensive learning-based anomaly detection, the proposed algorithm can efficiently detect anomalies by evaluating kurtosis and skewness of the time series. It proves to be both time and resource-efficient, making it suitable for real-time and resource-constrained scenarios.

articleTitle: Using an Evidence-Based Approach to Improve Calibration of Non-Domestic Building Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: In 2020, 24% of UK building emissions came from commercial and public buildings operations. Innovative methods are required to reduce energy demand and increase energy efficiency in this sector. Digital twin (DT) simulations prove valuable for this purpose, enabling the virtual testing of energy efficiency measures before implementing changes. However, the accuracy of DT simulations is only as good as their calibration's. This paper explores the advantages of using highresolution, disaggregated metered and occupancy data to improve DT calibration accuracy. The Andrew Wiles Building at the University of Oxford serves as a case study, with three different DT configurations created. The first and second use as-built and operational input data respectively, both with default occupancy. The third configuration encompasses observed operations and occupancy. Energy simulations run for the year 2022 are compared with the building's metered electricity use. The first two DT configurations result in monthly coefficients of variation of the root mean square error (CVRMSE) and normalized mean bias errors (NMBE) which are above ASHRAE Guideline 14's recommended threshold. In contrast, the third DT configuration falls right under the threshold, with a CVRMSE of 6.4% and NMBE of 5.0%, indicating a significant calibration accuracy improvement and showing the importance of accurate occupancy data in this area. Challenges related to missing data and uncertainties are also discussed.

articleTitle: A 31W High Efficiency X-Band Class-F/F-1 GaN High Power Amplifier for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: With the advent of GaN technology, the use of GaN based RF Solid State Power Amplifiers (SSPAs) has increased manifolds in satellite communications, radar applications and electronic warfare. But designing a highly efficient (e.g. Class-F and Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) High Power Amplifier (HPA) at high frequencies (i.e. 10GHz and above) still remains a daunting task. Considerations such as an accurate device model, parasitic effects, device selection, load and source Pull analysis, circuit topology, biasing techniques, input and output matching networks and thermal management make SSPA design a challenging endeavor. At higher frequencies (i.e. CBand and above), Class-F and Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> amplifiers are predominately developed using MMICs because transistor's internal parasitics affect the Harmonic Control Networks (HCNs). Therefore, in order to use a packaged device for Class-F design at X-Band, transistor's parasitics have to be extracted and embedded in the HCN design. This work presents the design and characterization of a 10 GHz GaN based 31W High Power Amplifier (in Class-F and Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> classes) for satellite and radar applications by embedding internal parasitics of Qorvos's TGF2979 transistor in the HCN. The paper discusses design considerations, presents simulation results for Class-F and Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> classes, compares the results with existing literature and concludes with the performance evaluation of the power amplifier using Keysight's Advanced Design System (ADS). The achieved efficiency for Class-F is 56% and that for Class-F<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> is 57.6; this is significantly greater than the efficiency achieved by Class-AB implementation of same transistor's evaluation board (i.e. 31.25%), in datasheet (i.e. 40.8% max.) and in available reference design [3] (i.e. 42.3 at 5.8 GHz%).

articleTitle: Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic System Social Acceptance in Saudi Arabian Residential Sector: Unveiling Public Sentiments a Survey Study
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Saudi Arabia has embarked on a transformative journey, transitioning from an oil-centric to an environmentally-focused economy. A recent initiative involves empowering house-holds to generate electricity through small-scale residential rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (RRSPV). Despite this, the uptake of RRSPV deployment remains notably low. Acknowl-edging that the social acceptance of solar energy is pivotal for a successful energy transition, this research explores the acceptance of rooftop solar photovoltaic (RSPV) systems within the residential sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Through a comprehensive survey study employing a cross-sectional, web-based pilot survey with 214 participants representing the six main regions of Saudi Arabia, the research sheds light on crucial insights. Results indicate a commendable level of awareness, with 71.4% of respondents familiar with RSPV. Additionally, 66.7% believe RSPV can contribute to achieving the Kingdom's Vision 2030 targets, while 83.8% anticipate benefits such as reduced energy bills and increased energy independence. Key barriers to RSPV adoption include a lack of awareness about local installation companies and uncertainties related to government policies or regulations. These findings provide valuable insights into prevailing sentiments, attitudes, and potential barriers, thereby informing strategies aimed at catalyzing the widespread adoption of sustainable energy solutions in Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Optimization for the Energy Separation Performance of Ranque-Hilsch Vortex
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: In this study, the energy separation effect of Ranque-Hilsch vortex is analyzed by computational fluid dynamics. The investigation of the variation characteristics of flow parameters such as temperature, pressure and streamline pattern of the vortex field is carried out on the basis of experimental validation. The effect of the vortex stopper structure on the heat production and heating efficiency of the vortex flow has also been evaluated. The results show that the static temperature and static pressure at different axial locations within the vortex field first grow and diminish with the increase in the number of vortex stopper blades. The rectification and obstruction effects of the vortex stopper on the vortex flow are balanced with each other in the case of a 6bladed vortex stopper. Therefore, the 6-bladed vortex stopper achieves the highest heat energy yield and the best heating efficiency. This work is expected to provide inspiration for efficient operation and structural optimization of refrigeration and heating equipment, and to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of energy conversion in thermodynamic systems.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Linear Arc PM Vernier Generator for Wave Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Ocean wave energy has progressively been acknowledged as the most sustainable and ecologically sound means of converting mechanical energy into electrical energy. This article proposes multiple distinctive linear arc generator concepts for converting wave energy into electrical power. This study successfully addresses the issues of high cogging force, low output power, massive size, and mechanical integrity by combining the concepts of arc and linear vernier machines. For varying PM volumes and slot/pole combinations, two separate designs with the same dimensions as the base design have been created and assessed. Analysis is done by successfully comparing the proposed designs with the conventional designs. Results show a 28.47 % increase in flux linkage for design M2, and a 32.50 % increase in flux linkage for design M4 as compared to the conventional design. Results demonstrate a 37.16% reduction of cogging force for design M1 and a 54.58% reduced cogging force for design M3 as compared to conventional design. The designs also possess reduced current densities as compared to conventional designs. Generator analysis of designs illustrated an increase of 86.14% of the increase in output power for design M4, 79.98% of the increase in output power for design M2, 6.22% of increase in output power for design M1, and 53.72% of the increase in output power for design M3, respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Microgrid Sustainability Through Adaptive Energy Management Using Intelligent Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: This study introduces an advanced control algorithm tailored for a bipolar DC microgrid to optimize the distribution of power among key resources, including wind energy generators (WEGs), solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, and battery energy storage (BES) units. The developed algorithm, a combination of intelligent load sharing and real-time monitoring, dynamically allocates power based on immediate demand. In this context, the main contributors of microgrid, such as wind energy, solar panels, and battery storage, collaborate seamlessly to share the load efficiently. By prioritizing renewable sources and adapting the battery's charge or discharge to meet diverse loads, this control algorithm ensures not only stability, but also sustainable and optimal performance in bipolar DC microgrid operations.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Grids via Nonlinear Interval Observer: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Identify individual False Data Injection (FDI) attacks in different intelligent networks. FDI attacks can circumvent conventional means of identifying corrupt data and interfere with the health assessment process. The rise of FDI attacks has introduced significant security vulnerabilities to smart grids. To address these important issues, A technique for detecting FDI attacks in various SG systems have been proposed. The interval observer is designed to precisely predict the Temporal condition of the internal physical structure based on development of the physical properties of the smart grid system. A detection criterion has been proposed to activate an alert if the remaining interval fails to include zero, considering the inner state boundary and the outer interference boundary. A sensor isolation algorithm based on a logical matrix for assessing attack characteristics is additionally proposed for introducing FDI attacks into sub-areas. Finally, we hope this article complements a series of recent review articles and fosters further research in this rapidly evolving area. And discussed our opinions on remaining challenges and future research directions in this area.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layered Trust Enhancing Consensus Mechanism for Decentralized Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: The decentralized energy trading platforms are being considered as the best alternate to the ageing power grid. These platforms have the ability to transform the energy sector entirely by enhancing sustainability, flexibility and efficiency. But due to decentralized operation, the reliability of the participating energy users, is still a questionable avenue in these sort of platforms. Immutability, transparency, and traceability of the created transactions are all reliability-enhancing features that may be ensured with the use of the distributed ledger technology such as blockchain. Additionally, by using a trust-based consensus method, both, confidence of the energy prosumers and the involvement of the energy consumers may be significantly increased. A trust-based consensus mechanism implemented using multiple layers been designed and developed in this research work, to facilitate the decentralized energy trading process. This secure and robust decentralised energy trading environment will help the decentralized energy trading process, its true potential. The proposed mechanism is resistant to cyber-security threats and it maintains the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive data being generated during trading process. It is evident from the results that such a consensus method will increase energy user participation and overall confidence, while still being secure from the prospect of cyber-security.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Distributed Energy Resources in Passive Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Energy demand is increasing drastically in all sectors around the globe. Many under developed countries are facing deficit of demand & supply, load shedding and power blackouts. Injection of Distributed Energy Resources in existing Distribution Network can support to meet the power challenges on one hand and impact of their integration can also influence the performance of weak, outdated and unbalanced distribution network. Optimal placement of DER can help to curb the deficit of power demand. Conventional Distribution Network is transiting from unidirectional power flow to bidirectional power flow. Introduction of Radial loop distribution network and automation of distribution system can help DISCOs to improve the reliability parameters like SAIFI and SAIDI index. A load flow analysis of radial distribution network is carried out using MATLAB Simulink. Integration of DER and radial loop distribution network is also analyzed. Optimum design and placement of DER can help to reduce burden on grid, improve the power quality, voltage profile and reduction in technical losses. This research work can help DISCOs for their up gradation as well expansion plans.

articleTitle: Load Scheduling Using Demand Response for Demand-Side Management in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: The advent of smart grids (SG) has provided residents the opportunity to incorporate renewable energy and demand response (DR) into the electricity market for optimal demand-side management (DSM). This study introduces a generic DSM model featuring an Energy Consumption Scheduler (ECS) to optimally schedule the operation of smart appliances. The ECS leverages various optimization algorithms, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Optimization Algorithm (GOA), Wind-Driven Optimization (WDO), and our developed Hybrid Genetic Wind-Driven Optimization (HGWDO) algorithm, to schedule the operation of smart appliances for DSM under real-time DR. One of the key challenges in efficiently integrating RESs into SG is their time varying and intermittent nature. This study employs batteries to smooth out fluctuations in RE generation. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach optimally solves DSM and achieves the desired objectives of utility bill payment, and peak-to-average demand ratio (PADR) minimization compared to existing models.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Transformer Health State in Distribution Network Based on Data-Model Combination and Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: This article presents a methodology for assessing the health status of transformers in distribution networks. The proposed approach integrates numerical modeling and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation in order to address the limitations of existing evaluation methods, such as high ambiguity and subjective weighting. To establish a comprehensive dataset, fault data and normal operation data of transformers are collected. Subsequently, specific evaluation indicators for transformers in distribution networks are selected. Membership degree models and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation weights are then determined. To enhance the accuracy of the model, an optimization objective function is formulated by incorporating the deviation between predicted and actual lifespans. This function is utilized to update the parameters of the membership degree model and the evaluation weights. Through reverse optimization using the dataset, the model parameters and evaluation weights are adjusted accordingly. Finally, the health status of the transformers is assessed by combining the model parameters with the optimized weights. The proposed methodology is further validated by analyzing dissolved gas data obtained from transformer oils in the distribution network. A comparative analysis with traditional three-ratio and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method based on entropy weight method results demonstrates that this approach significantly enhances the objectivity and accuracy of health status assessment for transformers in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Impact of Distributed Generation and Battery Energy Storage Systems on an Interconnected Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: This research describes the integration of Distributed Generation and Battery Energy Storage Systems into an IEEE 14-bus power system network, as well as the simulation of the effects of symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults and harmonics on the network during balanced, unbalanced, and no-load conditions. The paper will provide an elementary and detailed description of the network system used, power generation sources and the likely issues encountered, power stability concerns as they relate to power transmission and distribution to consumers, as well as consumer on-peak and off-peak usage situations on the network. It will also detail methods of improving the power quality and sustainability of our network system to withstand load demands, issues surrounding power transmission, and methods to integrate renewable energy. The Distributed Generation, which used only renewable energy, the Battery Energy Storage System, and the fault conditions were all simulated using the most efficient electrical engineering software, DIgSILENT Power Factory, and the results were used for the Load Flow (balanced and unbalanced) and harmonics analysis.

articleTitle: Distribution Feeder Reconfiguration Using Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm-Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Traditional power distribution systems encounter challenges due to day-by-day increasing demand and aging infrastructure, resulting in power losses, low end voltages and service disruptions. In response, distribution feeder reconfiguration (DFR) has emerged as a promising solution. DFR involves strategically adjusting the connection status of distribution feeders to optimize system performance, enhance reliability, and improve power flow characteristics. This research focuses on devising an effective DFR solution using an advanced Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm-based framework. By judiciously opening or closing switches, the proposed approach aims to achieve voltage profile enhancement and reduction in power losses. These improvements collectively elevate the overall performance, efficiency, and reliability of distribution systems. Validation of the proposed approach is conducted through MATLAB simulations on the widely recognized IEEE 33-bus test system. Optimal Power Flow (OPF) results, employing the novel Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA) are analyzed to assess the effectiveness of the proposed DFR strategy. Using AHA based DFR framework, power losses are reduced up to 33.355% with the improvement in minimum bus voltage of 4.033% (in p.u.).

articleTitle: Data-Driven Robust Optimization for the Operation Optimization of Industrial Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: Operation optimization of industrial power stations is a challenging task owing to the operational uncertainties associated with the variables and hyperdimensional system design. Thus, conducting the mathematical model based robust optimization for such large system is computationally prohibitive as well as expensive task. To this end, we have presented data-driven robust optimization framework that is built on machine learning based model (Data Information integrated Neural Network (DINN)) and nonlinear programming (NLP) technique. The robust optimization framework is applied for the operation optimization of 660 MW capacity power station. The DINN models are trained on the historical data of the industrial power station to model thermal efficiency, power and heat rate –three performance metrics of the power station. Extensive hyperparameters tuning and validation of the DINN models are carried out to select better predictive models for the three output variables. Later, multiobjective optimization problem is formulated to maximize thermal efficiency, power, and minimize the turbine heat rate by NLP technique. The estimated solution of the multi-objective function is perturbed by 10000 gaussian noise to evaluate the robustness of the estimated solution. The achieved robust solution offers optimal thermal efficiency of 42.11% and heat rate of 7642 kJ/kWh at power = 658 MW while the variance produced in the function remains less than 0.01 –the threshold can be set by the user. The proposed data-driven robust optimization framework presented in this paper can be a computational effective and cheap approach to conduct the operation optimization analytics of the industrial systems subjected to the various operational uncertainties.

articleTitle: An Adaptive PID Observer for Enhanced State Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: This work presents an adaptive proportional integral derivative control-based observer for enhanced state estimation of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) to resolve the issues of slow convergence, and sensitivity to nonlinearities in conventional observers-based methods. Control observers-based estimation methods are getting huge appreciation in already controller-packed battery energy storage systems and electric vehicles due to their low computational complexity and high reliability which are the two most desirable characteristics of any online state estimation method. The proposed observer is designed using an equivalent circuit model of LIBs due to its strong observability and a great trade-off between fidelity and complexity. After due analysis and error convergence demonstration, the proposed algorithm is validated against the experimental multiple driving datasets mimicking real-time driving conditions. Finally, an experimental testbench, using 58Ah CALB L148N58A cells whose parameters are experimentally identified by particle swarm optimization, is set up to verify the practicability of the proposed algorithm. Experimental results show better accuracy, enhanced resilience against nonlinearities, and five times faster convergence for the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Prediction of Condensation Heat Transfer of Passive Cooling Systems in Nuclear Power Plants through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: The accurate prediction of steam-air mixture condensation plays crucial role in managing severe accidents such as main steam line break (MSLB) and loss of coolant accident (LOCA) using passive cooling systems within nuclear power plant containment. However, this prediction task remains challenging due to the intricate characteristics of two-phase flow phenomena and the absence of comprehensive underlying physics. While numerous empirical correlations have been proposed to estimate steam condensation heat transfer coefficients (HTC), there is still a need for more precise and reliable models because of limited range of applicability. This study addresses this challenge through a multidisciplinary approach that leverages machine learning techniques on a large dataset collected from existing literature. A comprehensive dataset consisting of 2658 experiments collected from published sources is employed to develop the model. Five different machine learning models (ML), namely artificial neural networks (ANN), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF) and Adaboost are utilized to predict steam condensation HTC. The findings of this investigation illustrate the superiority of ML models, particularly the ANN, in accurately predicting steam condensation HTC with wide range of applicability. These ML models outperform traditional empirical correlation commonly used for such predictions. By leveraging the power of ML, this study provides a more accurate and reliable approach to estimating steam condensation HTC under air-inclusive conditions.

articleTitle: Towards Zero Trust Security for Prosumer-Driven Verifiable Green Energy Certificates
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: In response to the critical need for environmentally sustainable practices, green energy certificates have emerged as a key mechanism to prevent greenwashing and ensure the authenticity of renewable energy sources. While incorporating blockchain technology has significantly enhanced the trans-parency and verifiability of these certificates, it has also intro-duced a trade-off in terms of increased operational costs due to the added control mechanisms of the blockchain. This challenge led to recent advancements in the state-of-the-art blockchain-based framework for verifiable green energy certificates, integrating trustworthy registries to balance trust and operational efficiency to enhance feasibility for real-world deployments. Our paper extended the same framework to elevate the trust factor without incurring additional operational costs of blockchain. At the heart of our proposed solution is integrating Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI), a technology that bolsters the system's reliability and empowers users/devices with control over their digital identities. By harmonizing the strengths of the Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLT) of IOTA with the public blockchain of Concordium, our framework maintains the integrity and transparency of the green energy certification process. It propels the system towards zero-trust security by distributing trust from a few centralized registries to many decentralized prosumer meters.

articleTitle: Energy Recovery Using Regenerative Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Energy Conservation and Efficiency (ICECE)
abstract: In this era, one of the major trends in the automotive industry is the emergence of electric vehicles and the main challenge regarding electric vehicles is energy usage. Therefore, the entire world is taking steps to convert waste energy into useful energy. In this paper, such a shock absorber design is implemented in which the energy from the shock absorber is regenerated using a series of neodymium magnets and fed back to the vehicle battery using converters and boosters. The radial magnets are used to produce green electrical energy from the energy that is lost due to damping and different losses. Neodymium magnets, rods, metallic steel pipes, and coils are used in various symmetries to complete the research project. The rings of magnets are attached to the inner rod, which moves in linear motion within the rings of the coils. At the same time, the rings of the coils are placed inside the metallic steel pipe. This linear movement of the rod generates energy that minimizes environmental pollution and reduces carbon emissions. This research project uses a compact regenerative suspension system from which the maximum voltages of 35.7 mV are produced with 125 turns of coil and 36 neodymium magnets arranged in radial alignment ring magnets.
